title: What If a Dying Star Made a Universe, Not a Black Hole?
hook: A new theoretical study floats a wild alternative to the black hole: a collapsing star might birth a tiny dark-energy-filled universe inside itself, halting the crush before a singularity forms.
key_points: Standard theory says a massive collapsing star forms a singularity hidden behind an event horizon.
This proposal suggests the collapse could instead seed a tiny new universe inside the dying star.
Dark energy in that miniature cosmos would expand it, pushing back against gravity's inward crush.
The result would be a 'gravastar' — an exotic object that mimics a black hole without a singularity.
content_html: When a massive star runs out of fuel and collapses, textbook physics says the result is a black hole: matter crushed into a singularity — a point of infinite density — sealed off behind an event horizon. Singularities are where general relativity breaks down, so physicists have long suspected nature might have a way of avoiding them. One speculative idea reimagines what's hiding inside.
extra_html: According to a ScienceDaily report, a new theoretical study proposes that a collapsing star might not form a singularity at all. Instead, the collapse could trigger the birth of a tiny new universe inside the dying star. Driven by dark energy — the same kind of outward push thought to accelerate our own cosmos — this miniature universe would expand and resist gravity's inward crush, stopping the collapse short. From the outside, the object would still look much like a black hole, but with a calmer, singularity-free interior. Physicists call such a hypothetical object a gravastar (short for "gravitational vacuum star"). It's firmly in the realm of theory for now, but it's a vivid reminder that what really happens at the center of a black hole is still an open question.

related.title: Black Holes
related.hook: A black hole is a place where gravity wins so completely that nothing — not even light — can escape once it crosses the edge called the event horizon.

related.title: Supernovae & Neutron Stars
related.hook: When a giant star dies, its core collapses and its outer layers blast away in a supernova that can briefly outshine an entire galaxy — leaving behind something extraordinary.

flashcards.prompt: In standard theory, what lies at the heart of a black hole formed from a collapsing star?

choices.text: A singularity hidden behind an event horizon
A miniature star that keeps fusing hydrogen
Empty, flat space with no gravity

flashcards.explanation_html: Conventional general relativity predicts the collapse ends in a singularity — a point of infinite density — cloaked by an event horizon. The gravastar idea offers an alternative.

flashcards.prompt: In the gravastar proposal, what stops the star from collapsing all the way to a singularity?
flashcards.back_html: Dark energy inside a tiny new universe seeded by the collapse would expand outward, pushing back against gravity and preventing total collapse.
